evidence.text: roof
Phonosemantic compound. 宀 represents the meaning and 豕 represents the sound.
居也。从宀，豭省聲。

Oracle bone script: Phono-semantic compound (形聲 /形声, OC *kraː): semantic 宀 (“roof”) + phonetic 𢑓 (xiá, “male pig”). An archaic variant closer to the original drawing is 𡩀. See 𢑓 (xiá) for more. Similar to 冡.
Later the phonetic component have been corrupted to 豕, so Shuowen Jiezi erroneously analyzed it as Phono-semantic compound (形聲 /形声, OC *kraː): semantic 宀 (“roof”) + abbreviated phonetic 豭 (OC *kraː, “pig”).
All etymologies based on the modern version of the phonetic component (豕) are folk etymologies since they miss the original component (𢑓).
Cognate with Tibetan མཁར (mkhar, “castle; house”) (Schuessler, 2007).
嫁 (OC *kraːs, “to give a girl in marriage”) is the exoactive of 家 (OC *kraː, “house; household; family”).

For pronunciation and definitions of 家 – see 傢 (“stubborn, obstinate, intransigent”).
(This character is the simplified form of 傢).
 Notes:
Simplified Chinese is mainly used in Mainland China, Malaysia, and Singapore.
Traditional Chinese is mainly used in Hong Kong, Macau, and Taiwan.
Cognate with 姑 (gū).

evidence.field: 形義通解; 略說 and 詳解
evidence.text: The database describes oracle-bone and bronze forms with 宀 plus 豕, or a form it identifies with 豭; it calls 豭 phonetic, and also proposes that the graph evokes livestock kept at home. It reports oracle-bone uses for ancestral temple and family, and bronze uses for royal house/court and counted households. These are the database's analyses and reported uses, not a consensus established here.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫: 家

evidence.source: Ministry of Education, Taiwan, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.field: 說文釋形; 字樣說明
evidence.text: Records the Shuowen gloss and analysis 居也。从宀，豭省聲 and says the small-seal form was written that way; its regular-script form has 豕 below 宀. This supports the traditional analysis but does not establish it as the graph's earliest structure.
evidence.title: [A01026] 家 - Ministry of Education Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants

evidence.source: Shuowen.org, text of Duan Yucai's commentary on Shuowen
evidence.text: Shuowen gives 居也。从宀，豭省聲. Duan Yucai (Qing dynasty) questions this phonetic explanation and proposes instead that the graph originally meant a place for pigs, extended or borrowed for human dwelling. This is a historical alternative, not direct evidence that the pig-enclosure proposal is correct.
evidence.title: 說文解字「家」

evidence.source: Yea-chul Son, article record and abstract, KCI
evidence.text: The 2003 article argues oracle-bone and bronze 家 forms combine 宀 with 豕 or 亥 as an associative compound, and proposes the original sense ‘pig enclosure’, extended to human dwelling. It explicitly contrasts this with Xu Shen's phonetic account. Its abstract also says oracle-bone contexts already use 家 for human dwelling or household. This account conflicts with analyses treating a form related to 豭 as phonetic.
evidence.title: ‘家’字와 ‘族’字의 形義考

evidence.text: Reports oracle-bone and bronze forms with 宀 and 豕, or 豭, and says the depicted structure can express livestock being kept beneath a dwelling. This does not independently establish that a boar-name was the source of 家's pronunciation. No secure independent pronunciation of a proposed depicted animal or sign was verified in this research.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫: 家

evidence.text: The entry reports oracle-bone uses for ancestral temple and family; bronze examples for 王家 and for households counted as 家. A 2003 article abstract separately reports human dwelling or household use already in oracle-bone contexts. These references support early dwelling and social-institution senses, but this review did not inspect dated individual inscription images or establish a sequence among the senses.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫: 家

evidence.source: Baxter and Sagart, Old Chinese reconstruction list (2014)
evidence.field: U+5BB6 家; U+8C6D 豭 entries
evidence.text: The published list gives 家 jiā, Middle Chinese kae, Old Chinese *kˤra, gloss ‘household’; it gives 豭 jiā, Middle Chinese kae, Old Chinese *kˤra, gloss ‘boar’. This is one reconstruction system and makes a phonetic relationship plausible if 豭 is the relevant component, but it does not prove the graph's historical component analysis.
evidence.title: BaxterSagartOCbyRadStr2014-09-20

evidence.field: rows 1535–1536; character, Mandarin, Middle Chinese, Old Chinese, gloss
evidence.text: Exact rows: 家 jiā kae *kˤra household; 豭 jiā kae *kˤra boar. The host and proposed phonetic character have matching entries in this dataset. The externally inspected Baxter–Sagart list independently shows the same values. 𢑓 is not present in the inspected matching rows, so no Baxter–Sagart reading for it is asserted.
evidence.title: BaxterSagartOCbyRadStr2014-09-20

evidence.source: Unicode Consortium, Unihan Database Lookup documentation
evidence.text: Unicode describes its Unihan lookup as providing reading and meaning information for individual ideographs. The requested per-codepoint GetUnihanData pages for U+5BB6 and U+8C6D both failed to open in the web tool. Local readings are therefore recorded as local data, not as externally verified character-specific Unicode records.

evidence.text: Local exact rows give kMandarin jiā for 家 and jiā for 豭. The HSK extract covers 家 but not 豭; 豭's full local Unihan_Readings.txt row was checked. These are modern metadata readings, not evidence for an ancient phonetic relationship. Character-specific Unicode lookup URLs were attempted but inaccessible in this research session.

evidence.text: The entry describes 宀 as the roof/dwelling element in its account of the graph. It does not identify 宀 as a mere modern positional variant; the graph form contains the full component. No separate historical ancestor claim is made here.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫: 家

evidence.source: Academia Sinica, Chinese Etymological Database; Baxter and Sagart list
evidence.field: 家 entry; 豭 component reading comparison
evidence.text: The database calls 豭 a phonetic element in one analysis. The Baxter–Sagart list independently gives 豭 *kˤra and 家 *kˤra (both Middle Chinese kae); modern local Unihan data gives both jiā. This supports phonetic compatibility for 豭 under that analysis. It does not validate Wiktionary's distinct claim that oracle-bone 𢑓 was the phonetic form or that 豕 is a corruption of it; this research did not verify the identity and reading of 𢑓 from a primary paleographic source.
evidence.title: BaxterSagartOCbyRadStr2014-09-20

evidence.text: Describes 甲骨 and bronze forms as 宀 with 豕 or 豭, calls 豭 a phonetic element in one account, and also interprets the combination as livestock kept at home. Reports oracle-bone uses for ancestral temple and family; bronze uses for royal house/court, counted households, and personal names. These are the database's analyses and reported usages; they do not establish a single consensus account or a dated progression among senses.

evidence.text: Identifies oracle-bone 豭 as a male-pig depiction, reports an oracle-bone sacrificial use in 合集1526, and cites Shuowen and later texts for the word 豭. This supports an early animal word use but does not prove that the lower sign in 家 had that name or supplied 家's pronunciation.

evidence.source: Xu Shen, Shuowen Jiezi, text and Duan Yucai commentary
evidence.text: Shuowen records 居也。从宀，豭省聲. Duan Yucai questions how 豕 could be shown to abbreviate 豭 and proposes instead that 家 originally meant a place for pigs, extended or borrowed for human dwelling. This is a later historical hypothesis, not direct proof of the graph's earliest sense.
evidence.title: 說文解字「家」

evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants

evidence.text: Records the Shuowen analysis 从宀，豭省聲 and explains that the regular-script form writes 豕 below 宀. Lists a second Mandarin reading gū with citations for the honorific/familial senses also written 大家. Its account establishes what the dictionary records, not the graph's original construction.
evidence.title: [A01026] 家 - Ministry of Education Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants

evidence.field: 以豬成家; cited inscriptions and semantic analysis
evidence.text: Reports an oracle-bone 家 example as 合集13584, interprets it as a house over a side-view pig, and identifies a late Shang 家 clan emblem on 家戈爵, 集成08235. The article relates pig keeping to household/family meaning, while acknowledging the combined associative/phonetic account. It also quotes the Western Han 方言, chapter 8, for the regional word 豭, and reports oracle-bone use of 家 in ritual contexts. These are source interpretations and cited records, not a complete dated semantic sequence.

context.provenance: Base evidence consists of imported local JSONL excerpts. Source names identify upstream datasets; extraction may lose sense and language boundaries. Further external evidence and research activity are documented separately in the dossier.
editorial_rules: Write about the character's graphic history; distinguish it from the history of a spoken word.
Separate historical explanation from mnemonics. Do not infer history from modern shapes or readings.
Sources may repeat one another. A source count is not independent corroboration.
Treat Shuowen as a historical account, not automatic confirmation. Its generated English glosses are excluded.
Unrelated word senses may appear in Wiktionary excerpts. Do not merge them into a character origin.
Related-character evidence retains its record_character. Do not silently transfer a traditional form's components to a simplified form.
No glyph image has been visually inspected in this packet. Do not claim to have inspected one.
Explain missing evidence explicitly, especially for Japanese-created characters. A Chinese spelling pronunciation is not evidence for a Japanese origin.

gaps: No primary paleographic plate or excavation inscription image for the earliest 家 forms was visually inspected. The precise date and reading context of particular oracle-bone examples remain unverified; Late Shang dating is contextual, not a character-specific first-use date.

The claim that the original lower component was 𢑓 and later became corrupted to 豕 remains unverified. Sources reviewed instead report different analyses, including 宀+豕/亥 associative readings and 宀+豭 phonetic readings.

The actual word or object depicted by the earliest lower sign, and its ancient pronunciation, were not independently established. Matching reconstructions for 豭 and 家 do not establish the name of a depicted object or prove that object-name borrowing occurred.

The graphic stages between oracle-bone, bronze, seal, clerical, and regular forms were catalogued by reference sources but not assessed from images here; precise chronology of the alleged graphic corruption is unresolved.

Semantic reports distinguish dwelling, ancestral temple/family, royal house/court, and household-counting uses, but the sources inspected do not establish a complete dated pathway among house, household/family, professional/expert classifier senses, and grammatical suffix uses. Gloss lists were not treated as chronological evidence.

The local Unihan data was checked for kMandarin values of 家 and 豭, but required codepoint-specific official Unicode record pages could not be accessed. The general Unicode lookup documentation was inspected instead.
Local Baxter–Sagart data contains rows for 家 and 豭 but not a checked row for 𢑓; no reading is assigned to 𢑓.

The database's conflicting descriptions and the museum article's pig-pens interpretation do not settle whether 豕/豭 was semantic, phonetic, or both in the earliest graph. The dossier's claim that 𢑓 was the original phonetic sign later corrupted into 豕 was not verified from a primary paleographic source; no sound value for 𢑓 is claimed.

Although Baxter–Sagart gives the same Old Chinese and Middle Chinese reconstructions for 家 and 豭, this does not establish the name or pronunciation of any object or sign depicted by the earliest lower component. Therefore an object-name borrowing account remains unsubstantiated.

Sources report oracle-bone uses for ancestral temple, family, ritual contexts, and a house/dwelling interpretation; they cite identifiable examples such as 合集13584. Individual dated inscription images were not examined, and the order or semantic links among home, household, family, royal institution, counted households, personal-name use, and later professional suffix uses remain uncertain.

Graphic stages are documented by paleographic databases and labeled artifact records, but no complete series of 家-specific primary forms was retrieved for this review. The alleged graphic corruption chronology is unresolved.
Character-specific official Unicode Unihan lookup pages for 家 and 豭 returned internal errors in the browsing tool. Local dataset values are recorded only as local cross-checks.

No Xiaoxuetang-specific 家 glyph image was selected because its query response and exact form labels could not be obtained during this research session. The selected Commons form is a modern redraw and should not be represented as a photograph or artifact facsimile.

The acquisition findings mark the sole character-specific Commons image URL as HTTP 404 and unavailable for this run. The fresh search found no alternate image with both verified direct image URL and reusable provenance. oraclebone.org supplied image links but states all rights reserved; Xiaoxuetang's inspected page was only the database home and did not supply a 家-specific image or query record. Therefore no glyph image is proposed.
The National Palace Museum article discusses historical analyses and inscriptions but is not an alternate direct image candidate with established reuse rights in this research.

This focused check verifies the current MOE Pinyin readings and the dictionary’s traditional analysis. It does not resolve the separate historical question of whether the earliest lower sign in 家 was 豭 or had another identity.

limitations.text: No glyph image is selected because the available 家 redraw could not be retrieved, the inspected alternative is rights-restricted, and no character-specific image was available from the other inspected database.
